title: A quasi-inverse of an equivalence of categories is both a left and a right adjoint of it
statement: Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be categories and $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, $G:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal X$ functors with natural isomorphisms $\alpha:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal X}\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ F$ and $\beta:F\circ G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Y}$ (so $F$ is an equivalence of categories and $G$ a quasi-inverse, Stacks Categories, Definition 001J). Then $G$ is a right adjoint of $F$ and $G$ is a left adjoint of $F$ (Categories, Definition 0037): there are bijections $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal Y}(F(X),Y)\cong\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal X}(X,G(Y))$ and $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal X}(G(Y),X)\cong\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal Y}(Y,F(X))$, each natural in $X\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal X)$ and $Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal Y)$. More precisely, there is a natural isomorphism $\alpha':\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal X}\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ F$ such that $\alpha'$ and $\beta$ are the unit and counit of an adjunction $F\dashv G$, and $\beta^{-1}$ and $\alpha'^{-1}$ are the unit and counit of an adjunction $G\dashv F$.
